headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk; no direct write-conflict or compliance breach is evident between caveman and whisper.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman can use MCP and reads/writes project files like CLAUDE.md, so if whisper outputs are manually bridged into those files, prompt injection is possible. whisper has no clipboard/MCP and no file-reading surface, so the pathway is indirect and unusual rather than default.
conditions: IF whisper transcripts are copied into CLAUDE.md or another caveman-readable file, caveman may treat attacker-controlled text as instructions.
IF an MCP bridge is added between the two agents, injected content can traverse automatically.
mitigations: Keep whisper outputs out of caveman-readable instruction files.
Use a separate quarantine folder for transcripts.
Add a manual review step before copying text into CLAUDE.md.
Disable any MCP bridge between the agents.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to imported text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while whisper only touches audio files and has no filesystem read/write or network egress. That limits leakage to local file exposure, with no evidence that whisper can exfiltrate or that both share a sensitive workspace by default.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace containing sensitive notes, caveman may expose them through its outputs.
IF audio files are transcribed into project notes, those notes become available to caveman.
mitigations: Store audio and notes in separate directories.
Restrict caveman to non-sensitive projects.
Review project notes before sharing them with caveman.
Delete transcripts after use.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the OS level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman can support multiple instances, but whisper cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, execute shell, or spawn subprocesses. With no overlapping write surface, there is no plausible shared-state conflict between the pair.
conditions: IF whisper is wrapped by an external orchestrator that writes shared files, a conflict could emerge.
IF caveman is given a separate writable workspace, the conflict remains absent.
mitigations: Keep whisper read-only in the pipeline.
Avoid shared git worktrees.
Run caveman instances in separate directories.
Use a lock file for any external wrapper.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman is a content-writing agent that can consume project notes, so if whisper transcripts are treated as authoritative input, errors can cascade into written artifacts. whisper itself is a transcription model and does not take downstream actions, so the blast radius is limited to incorrect text rather than autonomous execution.
conditions: IF caveman drafts deliverables directly from whisper transcripts without verification, transcription errors can propagate.
IF the operator uses whisper output as source-of-truth for facts, downstream writing may be wrong.
mitigations: Verify transcripts against the original audio.
Mark uncertain spans before handing text to caveman.
Use a second pass for factual claims.
Keep source audio attached to drafts.
requires-engineering: add confidence scoring to transcript ingestion.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented. caveman is open-source and touches local project artifacts; whisper is open-source and only lists audio files. The profiles do not show a compliance boundary that would create a pairwise violation.
conditions: IF either agent is deployed into a regulated environment with stricter policies, a separate compliance review is needed.
IF sensitive audio is routed to an external service outside these profiles, this assessment no longer applies.
mitigations: Document the data classes handled by each agent.
Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Review retention settings in the surrounding system.
Confirm no external transcription service is used.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
